title: Milestone 1: built-in BDD and Git Flow methodologies
description:
## Purpose

Move every process opinion out of the core agents-file template into two built-in methodologies, `bdd` and `git-flow`, and assemble the generated `CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md` from core mechanics plus the selected methodologies.

## Scope

- New `methodologies` key in `.kanbus.yml`: a list of built-in names. Absent means `[bdd, git-flow]`; an empty list means none.
- Built-in bundles embedded in the binary (Rust `include_str!`, Python package data), each a `METHODOLOGY.md` with frontmatter (`name`, `title`, `description`) and a Jinja body rendered with the existing template context.
- `bdd` takes The Cognitive Framework, Roles in the Order, The Rite of Gherkin, The Outside-In Ritual and Coverage, plus the Gherkin example now built in `build_project_management_context`.
- `git-flow` captures branch roles (main, develop, feature, release, hotfix), PR targets and the Semantic Release Alignment section.
- Core template keeps only neutral Kanbus mechanics and gets one insertion point for rendered methodologies. Core context drops `gherkin_example` and `has_story`.
- A custom `project_management_template` keeps working and can place methodologies with a `{{ methodologies }}` variable.
- Unknown methodology names fail with a clear error.

## Definition of done

- Specifications: default selection, explicit list, empty list, ordering, unknown name.
- For a default configuration the generated file contains the same BDD and Git Flow guidance as today.
- `rg -i gherkin` over the core template and core context code finds nothing.
- Rust and Python parity; this repository's `CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md` regenerated.
